newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean police question suspects in killing.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean police question suspects in killing.

text.p: South Korean police have questioned two students suspected of beating a man who they thought was an informer and who later died, a police official said on Friday.
Police said the outlawed militant pro-Pyongyang student body Hanchongryon, which has led student riots in the city in the past week, turned over the two suspects at a police station on Thursday.
"The two students admitted they beat the late Lee Suk during an interrogation," he said. "We are extending our investigations as we believe some Hanchongryon leaders are involved in the case."
He said the two suspects told police that Lee was passed to them by a student with a mask, but they refused to elaborate.
Autopsy reports showed on Thursday Lee Suk, a 22-year-old worker, died as a direct result of the battering.
He had been beaten and his wrists roped together during a lengthy interrogation in the student union building to extract a confession that he was a spy, according to a Hanchongryon account.
The left-wing students group had already admitted responsibility for the violent death of the man whose badly bruised body was delivered to a hospital in Hanyang University on Wednesday.
Students demanding the resignation of President Kim Young-sam and details of his 1992 election spending went on the rampage last Friday.
Since then there have been frequent clashes between police firing teargas and militant students wielding metal pipes and hurling firebombs.
A riot policeman died during clashes around Hanyang University on Monday. His funeral was held on Thursday.
Prime Minister Koh Kun vowed to put an end to campus violence and ordered the arrest of Hanchongryon leaders by the end of June.
